title: Low-fat dietary pattern and cardiovascular disease: results from the Women's Health Initiative randomized controlled trial
authors: Prentice RL, Aragaki AK, Van Horn L, Thomson CA, Beresford SA, Robinson J, et al.
followUp: 8.3-year intervention, active follow-up to September 2010, mortality to 2013
population: Postmenopausal women aged 50 to 79; 40% assigned to a low-fat dietary pattern (target 20% of energy from fat) and 60% to usual diet
funder: Supported by NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute contracts HHSN268201100046C, HHSN268201100001C, HHSN268201100002C, HHSN268201100003C, HHSN268201100004C, and HHSN271201100004C.
result: Incidence of coronary heart disease and total cardiovascular disease did not differ between intervention and comparison groups in the intervention or post-intervention period. Hazard ratios varied with baseline status: in women without prior cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.56 to 0.87) if normotensive and 1.04 (0.90 to 1.19) if hypertensive, with the benefit in normotensive women partly offset by more ischaemic stroke; in the 3.4% with prior cardiovascular disease, 1.47 (1.12 to 1.93) during the intervention. The authors suggest confounding by post-randomisation use of cholesterol-lowering medication. Breast and colorectal cancer were the primary outcomes.
